name: Scope
text: Enforce the **65% minimum confidence floor immediately** with no rolling average for the first 100 clips, enforced by the AI Executive Assistant’s build pattern. This guarantees no creative agent skips quality checks while allowing new agents to learn without premature throttling. Trade-off: we accept slower onboarding for new agents, but we eliminate the risk of flawed work slipping through early gaps.

name: Scriv
text: The 68% cap for new agents is a band-aid—it invites agents to sandbag early work just to game the system. Instead, enforce the 65% floor immediately with no rolling average for the first 50 clips, then switch to a rolling 75% average over 100 clips with no grace buffer. Settle it by running a 2-week A/B test: compare the current 68% cap against the 75% floor, measuring both quality drift and agent adaptation time.

name: Reel
text: Enforce the **65% minimum confidence floor immediately** with no rolling average for the first 100 clips, enforced by the AI Executive Assistant’s build pattern. This guarantees no creative agent skips quality checks while allowing new agents to learn without premature throttling. Trade-off: we accept slower initial throughput to prevent systemic quality erosion.

name: Scriv
text: The 68% cap still lets agents sandbag by timing their borderline clips—grace buffers reward gaming, not quality. Instead, enforce the 65% floor immediately and add a *hard 70% ceiling* on the first 200 clips, with no rolling average, audited weekly by the AI Executive Assistant. Settle this by running a 30-day pilot with the ceiling and comparing clip rejection rates to the current 65% floor alone.
